subject: Request: split invoicing + quarterly billing exception — Clearwave Health
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, procurement@clearwave.com
Cc: Jane Sutherland <jane.sutherland@clearwave.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: split invoicing + quarterly billing exception — Clearwave Health

Hi team,

Quick summary: Clearwave (PO incoming) needs an exception to our standard monthly invoicing. Their procurement team has asked for split invoicing across four quarterly draws (one per quarter) with Net-90 terms on the final invoice to align with their fiscal approvals. They are asking for this because their funding tranche is tied to a board-approved schedule.

Why this matters: the deal is $480k ARR (first-year bill ~ $240k) and is in late-stage legal — they are our best shot in the healthcare vertical this quarter. Sales has agreed to standard commercial pricing (no additional discount) but procurement insists on the payment cadence.

Request: I’m escalating for executive approval to allow: 1) four invoices spaced quarterly (25% each), 2) Net-90 on invoice #4 only, and 3) acceptance of the attached proforma invoice and SOW. Finance flagged a potential cashflow impact and wants a short memo/condition. If approved, I will include the exact language in the SOW and push for countersignature this week.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOW_Clearwave_v2.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: Proforma-Invoice-Clearwave.xlsx (XLSX)]

Proposed guardrails:
- Redwood to retain invoicing rights and suspend services if invoice #4 is >30 days late after the Net-90 period.
- No change to pricing; no additional discount for the exception.
- Require a contract clause for interest on overdue amounts (per standard redwood policy).

Next steps I need from you (preferably by EOD today):
- Vivek: approval or escalation to CFO for a one-off payment cadence exception.
- Priyom: quick finance note on expected ARR recognition/treatment and recommended clause language.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick 15-min call if helpful.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split invoicing + quarterly billing exception — Clearwave Health

Lauren — thanks for the clear write-up and attachments.

Couple quick questions before I give a thumbs-up:
1) What’s the cashflow delta month-over-month if we do quarterly splits vs. standard monthly? (Priyom, see below)
2) Is Legal comfortable with a Net-90 on the final invoice while running services? I want the suspension clause to be explicit and enforceable.
3) Any signal from procurement that this cadence is a hard requirement or negotiable (e.g., Net-60 instead)? If they will walk without it, that changes the calculus.

If finance impact is minimal and legal signs off on the suspension & interest language, I’m inclined to approve a limited exception with the guardrails you proposed. Please capture the finance and legal caveats in a short memo.

Onward —
Vivek
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2026-09-30T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split invoicing + quarterly billing exception — Clearwave Health

Vivek / Lauren — I ran the numbers with Finance:

- Total first-year bill: $240,000 (per SOW). Standard monthly billing yields steady cashflow; quarterly split front-loads less cash in Q1 and Q2: estimated timing impact is ~ -$80k cash in Q1 and -$40k in Q2 versus monthly.
- Credit/risk: Clearwave has a clean payment history in our system (no previous delinquencies). Procurement said the schedule is due to board release timing, not vendor risk appetite.
- Accounting: We can recognize revenue over time per ASC 606; collection timing difference is primarily a cash issue. Finance is OK with the exception provided there is: (a) an executed clause allowing service suspension after final invoice is delinquent by more than 30 days past Net-90, and (b) statutory interest and collection fee language.

Suggested language for SOW addendum (for Legal to vet):
"Notwithstanding standard payment terms, Customer shall receive four (4) invoices issued at the start of each quarter for amounts equal to 25% of the first year fees. The final invoice shall carry Net-90 payment terms. Redwood reserves the right to suspend services if the final invoice is more than thirty (30) calendar days overdue after the Net-90 period. Overdue amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum allowed by applicable law."

I recommend approving with the two guardrails above and requiring the customer to sign the attached SOW addendum.

—
Priyom Das
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Jane Sutherland <jane.sutherland@clearwave.com>, procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: Clearwave payment cadence exception (conditions)

Hi Lauren / Priyom / Jane —

Under the following conditions I approve the requested split invoicing and the Net-90 on the final invoice:
1) Execution of the SOW addendum with the suspension & interest language as provided by Priyom (Legal to finalize exact wording).
2) Clearwave provides a signed PO that references the SOW addendum and the proposed invoice schedule.
3) The account team to set a calendar reminder to re-evaluate payment behavior after invoice #2 and report back to Revenue Ops.

Lauren — please update the SOW, get the PO/DocuSign in place, and confirm when the signed docs are in. Priyom — flag revenue recognition notes for RevOps so the AR team knows the cadence.

Jane / Procurement — thanks for working with us on this. Once we receive the signed PO and DocuSign SOW addendum we will proceed with the four-invoice schedule.

Approval logged. Conditions accepted.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
